attention_mechanism.definition: A weighted lookup in which each position combines values according to query-key similarity.

autocorrelation.definition: Correlation between the errors or observations of a process at different times.

backpropagation.definition: Applying the chain rule through a computational graph to obtain gradients for every parameter.

bias_variance_tradeoff.definition: The decomposition of expected prediction error into squared bias, variance and irreducible noise.

bootstrap.definition: Estimating the sampling distribution of a statistic by resampling the observed sample with replacement.

calibration.definition: The agreement between predicted probabilities and observed frequencies.

central_limit_theorem.definition: Standardized sums of independent variables with finite variance converge in distribution to the normal law.

cointegration.definition: Two or more integrated series sharing a stationary linear combination, i.e. a long-run equilibrium relation.

collider.definition: A variable caused by two others; conditioning on it creates association between them.

confidence_interval.definition: A random interval whose construction captures the true parameter in a stated proportion of repeated samples.

confounder.definition: A common cause of both treatment and outcome, which creates association without causation.

consistency.definition: An estimator is consistent when it converges in probability to the true parameter as the sample grows.

cramer_rao_bound.definition: The smallest variance any unbiased estimator can achieve, equal to the inverse of the Fisher information.

difference_in_differences.definition: Comparing the change over time in a treated group with the change in an untreated group.

endogeneity.definition: Correlation between a regressor and the error term, which makes least squares inconsistent.

exogeneity.definition: The assumption that the error term has zero mean conditional on the regressors.

false_discovery_rate.aliases: taux de fausses decouvertes|معدل الاكتشاف الكاذب|benjamini
false_discovery_rate.definition: The expected proportion of false positives among the rejected hypotheses.

fisher_information.definition: The expected curvature of the log-likelihood; it bounds how precisely a parameter can be estimated.

fixed_effects.definition: A panel estimator that removes every time-invariant unit characteristic by subtracting unit means.

gradient_descent.definition: An iterative optimizer that repeatedly steps against the gradient of the loss.

granger_causality.definition: Predictive precedence: past values of one series improve the forecast of another. It is not causation.

heteroskedasticity.definition: Error variance that changes across observations, invalidating the classical standard-error formula.

impulse_response.definition: The path of a variable's response over time to a one-off shock in a dynamic system.

instrumental_variable.definition: A variable that moves the endogenous regressor but affects the outcome only through it.

law_of_large_numbers.aliases: loi des grands nombres|قانون الأعداد الكبيرة
law_of_large_numbers.definition: The sample mean of independent draws converges to the expectation as the sample grows.

maximum_likelihood.definition: Choosing the parameter value that makes the observed sample most probable under the assumed model.

mediator.definition: A variable lying on the causal path from treatment to outcome; controlling for it removes part of the effect.

multicollinearity.definition: Near-linear dependence among regressors, which inflates coefficient variances without biasing them.

omitted_variable_bias.aliases: biais de variable omise|تحيز المتغير المحذوف
omitted_variable_bias.definition: The distortion of a coefficient caused by leaving out a variable that affects the outcome and correlates with the regressor.

ordinary_least_squares.definition: The estimator that minimizes the sum of squared residuals in a linear model.

orthogonal_projection.definition: The closest point to a vector within a subspace; the residual is perpendicular to that subspace.

p_value.definition: The probability, computed assuming the null hypothesis is true, of a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed.

parallel_trends.definition: The identifying assumption that treated and control groups would have moved together absent treatment.

posterior_distribution.definition: The updated distribution of a parameter after combining a prior with the observed likelihood.

potential_outcome.definition: The outcome a unit would have under a given treatment, only one of which is ever observed.

principal_component.definition: A direction of maximal variance in the data, given by an eigenvector of the covariance matrix.

r_squared.definition: The share of the variance of the dependent variable accounted for by the fitted model.

random_effects.definition: A panel estimator that treats unit effects as random and uncorrelated with the regressors.

regression_discontinuity.definition: Using a threshold rule that assigns treatment to compare units just above and just below the cutoff.

regularization.definition: Adding a penalty on coefficient size to trade a little bias for a large reduction in variance.

residual.definition: The difference between an observed value and the value fitted by the model.

roc_curve.definition: The set of true- and false-positive rate pairs traced as the classification threshold varies.

sampling_distribution.definition: The distribution of a statistic across all samples that could have been drawn.

shapley_value.definition: A feature's average marginal contribution to a prediction across all orderings of the features.

standard_error.definition: The standard deviation of the sampling distribution of a statistic.

stationarity.definition: A series whose mean, variance and autocovariances do not change over time.

statistical_power.definition: The probability that a test rejects the null hypothesis when a specified alternative is true.

type_i_error.aliases: alpha|false positive|erreur de type I|خطأ النوع الأول
type_i_error.definition: Rejecting a null hypothesis that is in fact true; its probability is the size of the test.

type_ii_error.aliases: beta|false negative|erreur de type II|خطأ النوع الثاني
type_ii_error.definition: Failing to reject a null hypothesis that is false; its probability is one minus the power.

unbiasedness.definition: An estimator is unbiased when its expectation equals the parameter it estimates.

unit_root.definition: An autoregressive root equal to one, so shocks accumulate permanently and the variance grows without bound.

volatility_clustering.definition: The tendency of large price changes to be followed by large changes of either sign.
